name: Engineering Canteen
did_you_know: Food waste from campus canteens is composted right here as part of the Green Campus Initiative.
info_md: Sits near the Engineering building's vermicomposting pits; food waste from campus canteens is composted right on site as part of the Green Campus Initiative. It gets packed at lunchtime, so come early or be ready to hunt for a seat.

name: Govindas Canteen
did_you_know: Runs on a "Three Foods" philosophy: food for thought, food for health, and food for the soul.
info_md: The design runs on a "Three Foods" philosophy: food for thought, food for health, and food for the soul, the idea being that eating should feel like an extension of learning, not a break from it. Architects deliberately focused on daylighting for this project: massive, open, sunlit spaces meant to filter in natural light, intended to lower stress and encourage a sense of peace while students study or eat. Unlike older college canteens that were just quick grab-and-go spots, the new layout was engineered as a collaboration hub — a space meant for lingering, working, and connecting, not just refueling.

name: Sports Canteen
did_you_know: Runs as a dedicated cafe inside the Eklavya Sports Complex, operated in partnership with Jimmy Boy.
info_md: Runs as a dedicated cafe inside the Eklavya Sports Complex, operated in partnership with Jimmy Boy. Its menu is dominated by cafe-style comfort items, continental snacks, and quick street bites.

name: Aurobindo Canteen
did_you_know: Its food waste feeds a biogas plant located right behind the canteen.
info_md: Its food waste feeds a biogas plant located right behind the canteen. The biogas generated isn't in active use yet, but the plan is to close the loop completely: waste from the canteen generates gas, and that same gas gets piped back to fuel the canteen's own cooking.

name: Kutchi Haveli
did_you_know: Built using "recycled" architectural parts salvaged from old buildings in Kutch villages.
info_md: The Haveli was built using "recycled" architectural parts salvaged from old buildings in Kutch villages that were being demolished for modern construction, preserving craftsmanship that would otherwise be lost. It reflects the Somaiya family's own roots: they're Kutchi Lohanas, and this heritage runs through several campus landmarks. Part of a wider Trust initiative that's also restoring old Kutch homes into village libraries (a project called Somaiya Pustakalaya).

name: Saraswati
did_you_know: Built with a central courtyard featuring a Tulsi plant and a water fountain, evoking the sound of a flowing river.
info_md: Built with a central courtyard featuring a Tulsi plant and a water fountain, meant to evoke the sound of a flowing river. On the outside stands a statue of Dariyalal, the Somaiya family's guardian deity as Kutchi Lohanas, also revered as Jhulelal by Sindhis and as Zinda Peer/Lal Shahbaz Qalandar by Sufis.

name: Sanskriti Vihara
did_you_know: Connected to the Somaiya Bharatiya Sanskriti Peetham, founded for deep study of Vedic religion and interfaith dialogue.
info_md: Connected to the Somaiya Bharatiya Sanskriti Peetham, founded to promote deep study of Vedic religion and interfaith dialogue. The building's layout is a modern reinterpretation of ancient Indian baolis (stepwells).

name: Basketball Court (Eklavya)
did_you_know: In 2026, Eklavya hosted the FISU World University Squash Championship.
info_md: In 2026, it hosted the FISU World University Squash Championship; Team India (both Somaiya students!) won an individual Gold, an individual Bronze, and a team Silver.

name: Table Tennis
did_you_know: An indoor arena with professional-grade tables and flooring for training and tournaments.
info_md: An indoor arena within the sports infrastructure, equipped with professional-grade tables and flooring to accommodate recreational sessions, training, and tournaments.

name: RIIDL
did_you_know: A technology business incubator supported by DST and DBT-BIRAC.
info_md: Research Innovation Incubation Design Labs (RIIDL) serves as a technology business incubator supported by DST and DBT-BIRAC. It provides startups with 24/7 access to workspaces, FabLabs, AI/ML labs, and seed funding support.

name: BIO RIIDL
did_you_know: India's first DIY Bio-Lab and incubator focused on life sciences and synthetic biology.
info_md: India's first DIY Bio-Lab and incubator focused on life sciences, biotechnology, and synthetic biology. It gives student innovators and early-stage bio-entrepreneurs access to specialized wet lab facilities, testing equipment, and bio-incubation grants.

name: Nakshatra Garden
did_you_know: Features plants arranged according to astrological constellations (Nakshatras).
info_md: Maintained by the project office as part of the Green Campus Initiative, featuring plants arranged according to astrological constellations (Nakshatras) with medicinal and religious significance.

name: Somaiya Statue Area
did_you_know: A landscaped green patch built around the memorial statue of founder Karamshi Jethabhai Somaiya.
info_md: A central landscaped green patch on campus built around the memorial statue of the founder, Karamshi Jethabhai Somaiya, offering a quiet seating spot under mature shade trees.

name: In front of Polytechnic
did_you_know: A popular student hang-out and event space outside the K. J. Somaiya Polytechnic building.
info_md: An open green lawn situated directly outside the K. J. Somaiya Polytechnic building, acting as a popular student hang-out and event space shaded by native trees.

name: Botanical Garden
did_you_know: Managed alongside the Department of Botany, housing a wide collection of plant species.
info_md: Managed alongside the Department of Botany, housing a wide collection of plant species, herbs, and flora used for student learning, research, and campus biodiversity conservation.

name: Biodiversity Garden
did_you_know: A dedicated ecological zone created to sustain local flora and fauna near the sports facilities and KJSIM.
info_md: A dedicated ecological zone near the sports facilities and KJSIM, created to sustain local flora and fauna, attract birdlife, and serve as a green lung for the campus.
